items.title: New studies bolster theory that viruses sparked complex life

featured_image.name: Giant viruses may be more alive than we thought

items.description: A pair of recent studies is reviving a long-debated question in evolutionary biology: did viruses help give rise to all complex life on Earth? The discovery of a new giant virus in Japan and fresh genomic evidence that ancient microbes could tolerate oxygen are together lending new weight to the idea that the cell nucleus — the defining feature of plants, animals, and fungi — may trace its origins to a viral infection billions of years ago.

items.title: UK considers removing Andrew from royal succession

featured_image.name: Why was former Prince Andrew arrested by UK police?

items.description:
The UK government is considering legislation to remove Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor from the royal line of succession, the BBC reported on Friday, a day after the former prince became the first senior royal in modern history to be arrested. The move marks a reversal from the government's position in October 2025, when Downing Street said there were "no plans" for legislative changes to the succession order.[1][2][3][4]

Andrew, 66, was arrested at Wood Farm on the King's Sandringham estate on Thursday morning — his birthday — on suspicion of misconduct in public office. Thames Valley Police said he was detained as part of an investigation into allegations that he shared confidential government information with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the UK's special trade envoy. He was held for approximately 11 hours at Aylsham police station in Norfolk before being released under investigation.[5][6][7][8]

items.title: Trump orders new 10% global tariff hours after Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA levies

featured_image.name: Trump says he will sign order imposing a 10% global tariff

items.description:
President Trump appeared in the White House briefing room on Friday afternoon flanked by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Attorney General Pam Bondi, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to deliver a defiant response to the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling that his sweeping tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act were unlawful. Trump called the decision "deeply disappointing" and announced he would immediately sign an executive order imposing a new 10% global tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, "over and above our normal tariffs already being charged".[1][2][3][4][5][6]

The announcement marks the administration's first concrete step in a contingency plan developed over months in anticipation of a possible court defeat.[7][8]

items.title: EU fails to agree on new Russia sanctions package ahead of war anniversary

featured_image.name: EU's Costa, von der Leyen to visit Kyiv on Feb. 24

items.description:
EU ambassadors failed to reach agreement on the bloc's 20th package of sanctions against Russia on Friday, with a proposed ban on maritime services for Russian oil tankers remaining the central obstacle as the fourth anniversary of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches on February 24.[1][2]

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas expressed confidence the package would still be adopted, telling reporters, "Next Monday, we aim to adopt the 20th sanctions package against Russia". Negotiations among ambassadors are expected to continue over the weekend before foreign ministers meet in Brussels on February 23.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Up to 20,000 unaccounted for after ISIS camp empties in Syria

featured_image.name: At the al-Hol camp in Syria for ISIS families, women are ...

items.description: U.S. intelligence agencies have concluded that between 15,000 and 20,000 individuals, including affiliates of the Islamic State, are now unaccounted for following a mass departure from Syria's al-Hol detention camp, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal citing U.S. officials familiar with the assessment. The finding underscores what analysts and Western diplomats have described as one of the most acute counterterrorism failures since the fall of ISIS's self-declared caliphate in 2019.[1][2]

items.title: Indie game publisher says TikTok ran racist AI ads without its consent

featured_image.name: Tunic, Night in the Woods Publisher Says TikTok Is Creating ... - IGN

items.description:
Finji, the independent game studio behind Night in the Woods and Tunic, has accused TikTok of using generative AI to alter its advertisements without permission, including one that introduced a racist, sexualized stereotype of one of the studio's characters. TikTok declined to comment on the record when contacted by IGN, which first reported the story.[1]

The dispute centers on ads Finji runs through TikTok for its games, including the upcoming title Usual June. According to Finji CEO and co-founder Rebekah Saltsman, the studio's TikTok ad account has all AI features disabled, yet AI-modified versions of its ads have been appearing on the platform as if posted directly from Finji's official account.[2][1]

items.title: Artemis II launch set for March 6 after fueling test successful

featured_image.name: Artemis II: NASA's First Crewed Lunar Flyby in 50 Years

items.description:
NASA is targeting March 6 as the launch date for its Artemis II mission after engineers successfully completed a critical fueling test of the Space Launch System rocket on the evening of February 19, overcoming hydrogen leak problems that had derailed an earlier attempt and delayed the historic crewed journey to the moon.

The four-member crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialists Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen — began preparing to enter a roughly 14-day quarantine on February 20 in Houston, a step NASA said would "preserve flexibility in the March launch window."[1]
